title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Film Non-Uniformity Detection on Archer 700
subtitle: Pre-Diffusion Quality Validation for 45nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Wei Zhang

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Archer 700 system to detect and classify Film Non-Uniformity defects during pre-diffusion inspection at the 45nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Film Non-Uniformity defects that are critical to yield at the 45nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Archer 700 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Archer 700
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Film Non-Uniformity
- Process Step: Pre-Diffusion
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 45nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all Archer 700 systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for pre-diffusion monitoring in the 45nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Archer 700
Software Version: v8.1.544
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_45nm_PRE_DIFFUSION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (172 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Archer 700 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Film Non-Uniformity defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 45nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 58 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.7% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-18
Wafers Tested: 41
Total Defects Found: 360
Defect Density: 114.59 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 1.7%
Capture Rate: 94.3%
Test Duration: 278 minutes
System Uptime: 96.3%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Archer 700 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Film Non-Uniformity at the 45nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
